sources.entry: Helix - Free, open-source and private alternative to GraphPad Prism for scientific statistics and publication-ready graphs, powered by R.

summary.one_liner: Helix is a free, open-source, macOS desktop app for organizing scientific data and producing statistical analyses and publication-ready graphs, using R (via webR) and Plotly.
summary.what_it_does: Helix organizes data into tables of five types (Column, XY, Grouped, Multiple Variables, Contingency), each holding its own analyses and graphs that update when values change. Statistical tests are run by R compiled to WebAssembly through webR, including t tests, ANOVA variants, Kruskal-Wallis, Friedman, post-hoc comparisons, two-way ANOVA, and 4PL dose-response curve fitting. Graphs are drawn with Plotly.js and can show significance stars or P values, regression lines, and fitted curves, with styling controls for colors, points, error bars, and layout. Results and graphs can be exported as PNG, JPG (at 150, 300 or 600 DPI), or SVG, or copied into Keynote, PowerPoint or Word. Projects are saved as plain-JSON .hlx files described in FILE-FORMAT.md, and the app states that all data stay on the Mac with no telemetry, apart from a daily check for updates on GitHub.
use_cases: analyze lab experiment results with t tests or ANOVA
make publication-ready graphs for a scientific paper
fit dose-response curves and calculate EC50
run statistics on grouped or time-course data
replace GraphPad Prism on a Mac
export graphs at print resolution for journals
how_to_run: Download the Helix_…_aarch64.dmg (Apple Silicon) or Helix_…_x64.dmg (Intel) from the Releases page
Open the DMG and drag Helix into the Applications folder
To build from source: install Node.js 24 or later, Rust, and Xcode Command Line Tools
npm run dev (run with live reload)
npm run build (build the two DMGs)
notable: Every statistical result is computed by R, with tests checked against reference results via npm test
Guided analysis assistant that picks the right test based on pairing and normality questions, with optional Shapiro-Wilk check
Project files are plain JSON (.hlx), so data are not locked in
Built-in Sample Project showing every table type, analysis and graph
Runs entirely on the Mac with no telemetry
caveats: Building from source needs Node.js 24+, Rust, and Xcode Command Line Tools, plus both Mac Rust targets for the DMG builds
Only a daily update check connects to GitHub; the README does not describe other platforms
